predecessors.name: Chenla
predecessors.text: the southern half of the divided Chenla, on 'the Tonle Sap area in Cambodia', linked to the Mekong Delta

successors.name: Srivijaya
successors.text: 'incorporated into the Javanese monarchy around the year 790' (Chenla page); 'much of the area fell under the orbit of the Shailendra dynasty of Srivijaya' (Jayavarman II page)

successors.name: Khmer Empire
successors.text: the southern lands taken by Jayavarman II from Vyadhapura and Sambhupura up the Mekong; the Khmer Empire from 802

ledger.x: c. 707: Chenla splits and Water Chenla forms in the south. 'shortly after 706, the country was split into Land Chenla and Water Chenla' (New Book of Tang), after 6 February 707 by the Tang histories; 'Water Chenla is situated on the Tonle Sap area in Cambodia'.

c. 790: the Javanese hold ends the fighting. 'incorporated into the Javanese monarchy around the year 790' (Chenla page infobox 'Javanese invasion: 790'); the Jayavarman II page puts Jayavarman II on the throne as the Javanese vassal.

c. 790: Water Chenla ends under Java. Its last king 'seems to have been killed' and the polity was 'incorporated into the Javanese monarchy around the year 790'. The Jayavarman II page instead has him 'King of Lower Chenla' c. 780-802 as a vassal of Java; the two pages are reconciled as a Javanese dependency, drawn in…

wars.name: Javanese (Shailendra) attack on Water Chenla (780-790)
wars.outcome: A naval attack on Kumbhupura in 780; Mahipativarman killed; Water Chenla 'incorporated into the Javanese monarchy around the year 790' (Chenla page) with Jayavarman II as the Javanese vassal.

wars.name: Jayavarman II's defeat of a Cham army (790)
wars.outcome: The Sdok Kak Thom inscription says Jayavarman II 'defeated a Cham army in 790'; the page names no place and no change of border.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a frontier; the Tonle Sap, Mekong Delta and Champa edges of the outline are approximate.
